headline: Whitewater Permits and State Park Reservations
reservation: A launch permit is required for all river trips on the Lower Youghiogheny; these can be reserved via the PA State Parks system. Lodging at Kentuck Campground or park cabins often books out 6–11 months in advance. Separate tickets are mandatory for nearby architectural sites like Fallingwater and must be secured via the Western Pennsylvania Conservancy.

days.title: River Views and Cascading Water
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Ohiopyle Falls
stops.detail: Observe the 20-foot drop of the Youghiogheny River from the designated town-center overlooks.

stops.name: Cucumber Falls
stops.detail: Descend the stairs to view one of the most photographed waterfalls in the Laurel Highlands.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for local park roads; parking at Cucumber Falls fills rapidly.
days.note: Walkways near waterfalls can be slippery; stay on marked stone steps and paths.

days.title: Gorge Exploration and Rail Trails

stops.name: Great Allegheny Passage
stops.detail: Bike a scenic out-and-back section of this former railroad along the river gorge.

stops.name: Ferncliff Peninsula
stops.detail: Hike the loop trail to see unique botanical communities in a deep river bend.

days.driving: Walking or biking from town is primary; allow 2-4 hours for trail activities.
days.note: The GAP is a shared-use trail; yield to pedestrians and maintain controlled speeds.

days.title: Laurel Highlands Heritage

stops.name: Fallingwater
stops.detail: Tour the Frank Lloyd Wright masterpiece integrated into the Bear Run landscape.

stops.name: Meadow Run Natural Waterslides
stops.detail: Observe the unique sandstone formations carved by water over thousands of years.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for regional transit; mountain roads are winding with variable cell service.
days.note: Fallingwater tours require strict arrival times; allow extra time for check-in.

intel.title: Whitewater Regulations
intel.text: River access is strictly managed; do not enter the water above the falls. Guided tours are recommended for those without significant Class III-IV experience.

intel.title: Town and Trailhead
intel.text: The main visitor center lot fills by noon on summer weekends. Use the Ferncliff or Cucumber Falls overflow lots if the central area is congested.

intel.title: River Levels
intel.text: Check the Youghiogheny gauge levels at the visitor center before any paddling activity. High water after heavy rain can lead to temporary river closures.

intel.title: Regional Services
intel.text: Fill your tank in Uniontown or Farmington before heading into the park interior. Ohiopyle village has limited amenities compared to these gateway hubs.

intel.title: Laurel Highlands Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect total loss of signal along river sections and deep forest trails. Carry a physical park map obtained from the visitor center for safety.

plan.arrival: Drive from MGW or PIT; stock up on supplies in Uniontown before entering Ohiopyle village.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for main park roads; winter travel requires 4WD due to Laurel Ridge snow.
plan.goldenHour: Tharp Knob Overlook for sunset views of the river gorge; check seasonal gate hours.
